newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: IPC's German unit Hagenuk plans listing.
newsitem.headline: IPC's German unit Hagenuk plans listing.

text.p: Germany's Hagenuk Telecom GmbH, partly owned by Singapore's IPC Corp, is planning to list in the United States or on one of Europe's markets to fund its expansion plans, the Business Times said on Tuesday.
"We want to tap the equity market so that we can aggressively ramp up the production of Hagenuk," BT quoted IPC chairman Patrick Ngiam as saying in Hanover, Germany.
It said the listing could take place within the next 12 months.

IPC owns a 37.5 percent stake in Hagenuk, which makes telecommunications equipment. Ngiam was also quoted as saying at a technology fair that IPC intended to increase its stake in Hagenuk to more than 50 percent in the next few weeks.
"The initial public offering is purely an exercise to accomplish Hagenuk's overall growth plan. It is not an exercise shareholders take to exit from the company," Ngiam said.
The goal was for Hagenuk to carve out a 10 to 20 percent global market share in providing telecommunication solutions and equipment, Ngiam said.
Last week, London-based venture capital company 3i Group plc took a 12.7 percent stake in the company.
Ngiam said discussions were under way to bring in one or two venture funds from the United States to take small stakes in Hagenuk.
Other shareholders of Hagenuk are Manfred Schmitt, founder of German PC retailer Escom with a 37.5 percent share, Hongkong's Keeneast and Malaysian contract manufacturer Tru-Tech with minor stakes.
Hagenuk president Patrick Bouju said he was getting the company's research and development department to come up with a new product every six weeks.
Hagenuk makes a range of telecommunications products and develops its own chip technology.

Production at its Kiel plant in Germany is being increased to 1.5 million units of GSM (Global System for Mobile Communications) mobile phones a year and 1.2 million DECT (Digital European Cordless Telephome) and 500,000 ISDN (Integrated Services Digital Network) products annually, the Business Times said.
